title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1LC0LA_---1RD_1RF1RE_1LF1RD_1LB0RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1LC0LA_---1RD_1RF1RE_1LF1RD_1LB0RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the passes over the regular left part, two passes in the irregular part and the halting situation (kernel), and no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps.

What it does. The head sweeps the whole tape. Seen from the left end the tape is 0 (011)4 (1011011011)k followed by an irregular region. k grows steadily, about 14 copies per hundred new cells at the left end (k = 21 at step 103,296, 172 at 6,990,882, 329 at 24,861,720), while the irregular region stays between about 150 and 430 cells long. So all the growth of the tape ends up in the regular part; the irregular part acts like a machine that produces copies of the word.

Where a halt would come from. Only C reading a 0 halts, and C is entered only from B reading a 0 (writing a 1 and stepping left); so 0 B>0 halts (halt_B). In the run B reads a 0 only with a 1 to its left.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 21,748 cells have been visited and 15,177 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.52). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.411).

claims.title: Every way to a halt
claims.text: Two steps before any halt the machine is in 0 0 F>0; no other configuration halts within three steps.

claims.title: Passes over the left part
claims.text: E moving right rewrites each copy of 1101101101 as 1011110110, 12 steps a copy, and A moving left rewrites it back (one cell shifted), 50 steps a copy, for any number of copies.

claims.title: Passes in the irregular part
claims.text: D moving right turns each 011 into 101; B moving left turns each 101 into 100.

claims.title: The halting situation
claims.text: 0 B>0 halts after two steps; it is the only way into C reading a 0.

claims.title: Regular part grows, irregular part does not
claims.text: At every hundredth new cell on the left, up to 2.5·107 steps, the tape is 0 (011)4 (1011011011)k plus an irregular rest; k goes from 21 to 329 while the rest stays between 156 and 426 cells.

claims.title: Never close to halting
claims.text: In the first 10<sup>6</sup> steps B reads a 0 about 31,000 times, always with a 1 to its left.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The irregular part has not been described; the next step is to find how it hands copies of the word to the left part, or a set of patterns for it that is closed under the machine.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. A crystal of a ten-cell word grows on the left of the tape, fed by a disordered region on the right that never grows. This page runs it in your browser.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 21,748 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A crystal and its feeder
html: Compress the tape into repeated words each time the head reaches a new cell at the left end. At step 1,160,914 it starts

The first part is regular: the 10-cell word 1011011011 repeated. After it comes an irregular region with short runs of three-cell words. Counting at every hundredth new cell on the left, the regular part has 21 copies at step 103,296, 72 at 1,160,914, 172 at 6,990,882 and 329 at 24,861,720, while the irregular rest has between 156 and 426 cells the whole time. Every new cell of the tape ends up in the regular part.

The sweeps over the regular part are exact rewrites: E moving right turns each 1101101101 into 1011110110 in 12 steps, and A moving left turns it back in 50 steps (pass_right, pass_left). In the irregular part the head crosses runs such as 011 011 011, which D turns into 101 101 101 in nine steps (cross_D).

The only halt is 0 B>0 (halt_B): B writes a 1 and steps left onto a 0 in state C, which has no transition for 0. How the irregular region keeps its size and passes copies of the word to the left is the open question.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.52). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.411).
After 109 steps the tape spans 21,748 cells (10,827 left of the start, 5,225 right), with a density of 1s of 0.698.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: growing periodic part fed by an irregular region of bounded size
summary: A regular left part, the 10-cell word 1011011011 repeated, grows by one copy every few round trips, while an irregular right part of 300 to 430 cells keeps roughly the same size and feeds it. Open.
